references.title: Breaking the rules: bacteria that use several DNA polymerase IIIs.
references.assessment: Narrative review distinguishing bacterial C-family replicases from the damage-induced ImuC system. Polymerase fold does not identify which replication role a member performs.

references.title: Sending out an SOS - the bacterial DNA damage response.
references.assessment: Comparative SOS review documents lineage-specific regulons and alternative TLS systems, supporting optional RecA/LexA context and taxon-specific cassette assessment.

references.title: Myxococcus xanthus translesion DNA synthesis protein ImuA is an ATPase enhanced by DNA.
references.assessment: Purified Myxococcus ImuA has DNA-enhanced ATPase activity and DNA binding. These tested activities invalidate a universal no-activity statement, but do not establish the same activities in the existing Caulobacter, Pseudomonas or mycobacterial exemplars.

references.title: ImuA Facilitates SOS Mutagenesis by Inhibiting RecA-Mediated Activity in Myxococcus xanthus.
references.assessment: Myxococcus ImuA interacts with RecA1 and suppresses its recombinase activity. The study did not detect ImuA DNA binding; the later positive assay must be interpreted with this negative result rather than erasing it.

references.title: Investigating the composition and recruitment of the mycobacterial ImuA'-ImuB-DnaE2 mutasome.
references.assessment: M. smegmatis live-cell recruitment and biochemical evidence support an ImuB clamp-associated assembly role. Co-localization alone does not establish an active complete mutasome or native M. tuberculosis dynamics.

references.title: The RecA-NT homology motif in ImuB mediates the interaction with ImuA', which is essential for DNA damage-induced mutagenesis.
references.assessment: M. smegmatis ImuA′-ImuB structural and biochemical work refines accessory-complex assembly; organism-specific structure and functional tests do not establish universal ImuA-family ATPase chemistry.

references.title: New insights into the structures and interactions of bacterial Y-family DNA polymerases.
references.assessment: Computational comparative analysis distinguishes Y-family catalytic proteins from inactive ImuB and predicts interaction relationships. Predictions are not direct complex measurements.

references.title: Diversity and distribution of bacterial DNA polymerases.
references.assessment: Large comparative polymerase survey supports distinguishing DnaE2 from DnaE1/DnaE3/PolC and reports variable proofreading signatures. Predicted assemblies and genome co-occurrence do not prove complete cassette capacity.

references.title: Widespread distribution of a lexA-regulated DNA damage-inducible multiple gene cassette in the Proteobacteria phylum.
references.assessment: Comparative primary survey of lexA-associated damage-inducible cassettes. Regulation and distribution in its surveyed taxa do not establish universal operon organization.

references.title: An SOS-regulated operon involved in damage-inducible mutagenesis in Caulobacter crescentus.
references.assessment: Caulobacter primary genetic study; experimental NA1000 is a CB15 derivative. Cassette epistasis and mutational profiles support a cooperating route; ImuA molecular activity remains unresolved in this target.

references.title: Essential roles for imuA'- and imuB-encoded accessory factors in DnaE2-dependent mutagenesis in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
references.assessment: Mycobacterial genetics and interactions: distinguish M. tuberculosis cassette deletion/Y2H protein origin from M. smegmatis individual deletions and catalytic/clamp functional experiments. Cached full-text metadata does not guarantee complete Results/Methods; consultation records publisher verification.

references.title: Study of involvement of ImuB and DnaE2 in stationary-phase mutagenesis in Pseudomonas putida.
references.assessment: P. putida stationary-phase mutagenesis study; antimutator effect is bounded to its base-substitution assay and does not refute induced mutagenic activity under other conditions.

references.title: DNA Polymerases ImuC and DinB Are Involved in DNA Alkylation Damage Tolerance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Pseudomonas putida.
references.assessment: Pseudomonas alkylation-damage and mutagenesis study; P. putida PaW85 is described as isogenic to KT2440. Distinguish strain, damage and growth context; ImuC-dependent mutagenesis complements rather than contradicts the stationary-phase study.

references.title: DinB (DNA polymerase IV), ImuBC and RpoS contribute to the generation of ciprofloxacin-resistance mutations in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
references.assessment: P. aeruginosa genetic contribution to resistance-mutation yield. Outcome-specific perturbation evidence supplements cassette biology but does not establish a novel catalytic activity or a universal response.

references.title: DnaE2 polymerase contributes to in vivo survival and the emergence of drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
references.assessment: M. tuberculosis DnaE2 genetics links damage-induced mutagenesis and survival. Infection and resistance outcomes are downstream context, not additional molecular functions of the polymerase.

review_classification_note: PMID21475246 is labeled review on the publisher PDF, read via the author institutional repository, despite the machine cache classification PRIMARY_RESEARCH. Cached metadata is preserved.
pending: Resolve Myxococcus experimental protein to a primary-source locus/accession before adding a concrete representative.
step_evidence: Review and comparative evidence is placed at regulatory nodes, ImuA/ImuA-prime accessory nodes, ImuB assembly, and DnaE2 synthesis; broad module evidence remains as context.
